recipes.name: Thai Curry Soup
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup peeled and deveined medium shrimp

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add rice noodles and cook until tender yet firm to the bite, about 3 minutes. Drain and rinse well with cold water to stop the cooking; set aside.

Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in garlic, lemongrass, and ginger; cook and stir until aromatic, 30 to 60 seconds. Add curry paste and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in about 1/2 cup chicken broth and stir until curry paste has dissolved, then add soy sauce, sugar, and remaining chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover partially and simmer for 20 minutes.

Stir in coconut milk, spinach, shrimp, mushrooms, cilantro, and lime juice. Increase the heat to medium-high and simmer until shrimp are bright pink on the outside and the meat is opaque, about 5 minutes.
To serve, place some rice noodles into each serving bowl and ladle soup over the top. Garnish each bowl with a sprinkling of sliced green onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Thai Curry Soup
raw_recipe.description: This Thai curry soup features juicy shrimp, meaty mushrooms, tender spinach, and rice noodles in a coconut milk-based broth brightened with lime juice.

review.reviewBody: I added wedges of red onion and tomato. I left out the cilantro. I wanted it to taste like the thai curry soup at noodles and company. I think I succeeded.

Some tips for those wanting to rev up spice and flavor: mince or grind up a thai chili or 2 for spice and sauté with garlic in step 2. Also, if you have access to the ingredient, recommend palm sugar in replacement of sugar. Palm sugar makes a huge difference! Lemongrass adds flavor to the broth. I prefer to cut in large pieces, pound to release oils just a bit, and simmer lemongrass in broth for 20 minutes in step 2. I remove the lemongrass after as lemongrass is a tough stem to soften for consumption. I like to garnish with a little thai basil. A splash of fish sauce will do wonders as well!

Very tasty. I did do a few thing different. It makes a great base soup to add so many different ingredients. I made the broth up to the paste then added chicken strips. Also added the juice of 1/2 lime. Simmered for 30 minutes. Added the coconut milk as well as 2 tablespoons of basil. Let simmer for about 10 minutes to let the flavors blend. This was the basis for lunch time soup for the week. I would divide up into containers and freeze. When ready, I would thaw, heat up and add stir fry vegs and or shrimp. The flavor of the base was as good as you get in a really good Thai restaurant. Thanks for a new favorite.

Excellent recipe that can easily be made Vegan. I used extra firm tofu cut up into small cubes instead of shrimp and vegetable broth instead of chicken broth. Left out the spinach but added julienned carrots in the initial saute of garlic and lemon grass. Definitely use the lemon grass! It's SO worth the flavor! Added a dash of crushed red pepper flakes to add a touch more heat. Didn't use the noodles but ladled over Jasmine rice. Delicious! I will make again and again.

We loved this soup. It was full of flavor. I added 1/2 teaspoon of cayenne pepper because we like spicy, but it would have been delicious without I am sure. I didn't have fresh lemongrass so I used some dried. I put it in the broth and let it cook until we were ready to eat, then removed it. I will make it again but will sauté the mushrooms prior to putting with the other ingredients. Great recipe.

I have made this soup many times. One thing I do to take it up a notch. I take the shrimp shells and sauté them with spices and add some chicken broth and simmer for 20 minutes and make what I call the golden broth. Really adds a lot of rich flavor. I also add an andouille sausage to spice it up.

It was excellent as a starting point, but changes had to be made due to allergy to mushrooms, and spinach due to dislike.
Boy Choy leaves were substituted and stalks to the place of the mushrooms. Red curry was increased for more heat. Also, homemade broth was used, and the amount of shrimp was added too (about 170 grams. I cooked the shrimp separately, and husband likes his shrimp firm. Adding it and cooking for only 5 minutes was not sufficient for him.

Great recipe, tasted like restaurant Thai curry soup, Yum! The only change I felt I needed to make for flavor was instead of 2 teaspoons of red curry paste, I used 2 tablespoons. It needed that extra punch, though it was still not two spicy. Still very mild. We chose to use chicken instead of shrimp, because we love chicken curry. We prefer dark meat chicken, so used 1.5 lbs of chicken legs instead of shrimp. We also used fresh spinach, putting in a large 10 ounce container of fresh baby spinach. Will definitely make again. Thanks for a great recipe!

Great recipe. I made some alterations for personal preference: Fresh basil instead of cilantro, and veg broth instead of chicken broth. I also added fish sauce, it's in most Thai soups. I used baby portabella mushrooms (they cook nicely and aren't expensive) I've also made a few more times with bamboo shoots, baby corn, bell peppers, peanuts and more. Tasted great every time.

I added celery, carrots and zucchini while cooking, then puree'd it to thicken it some and to add more veggie nutrition. 
It tastes great as a soup. You can also add cut onions, peppers, potatoes, carrots, pumpkin, meat, etc and serve it with rice as a traditional curry.
I added a jalapeño and sautéed it with the garlic, ginger and lemongrass. I also subbed some chopped rotisserie chicken for the shrimp. This is easily the best soup I've ever made. Loved it!

Due to my limited pantry, I used 5 small cloves of garlic, 3 2inch pieces of dried lemongrass, 16oz chicken broth, 16oz beef broth, 1 can full fat coconut milk, 4 tbsps each of red curry paste and soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and dried cilantro. Easy and so delicious! Didn't have any protein to add in but it still was filling and fantastic. Done in 30 minutes!

Due to a purchase error I had Thai ribbon noodles on hand and found this recipe as way to use them. Many of the ingredients are not in my pantry so I started a grocery list. The $31.32 total, $7.83/portion is twice our budget. For a recipe that after 18 years on the site has only 279 ratings. The lesson learned is to note the popup from a sponsoring grocery advertiser citing the cost to purchase ingredients before spending my time.

Made it with a bit more shrimp because I had more on hand and this soup turned out wonderfully. I started with a turkey broth base and added chicken bullion for salt and a bit more flavor. I was a bit worried that it was going to be too spicy for others on my family, but once I added the mushrooms and spinach and noodles, it really mellowed out. The flavors are complex and savory. I love having spinach and noodles. I will be making it again, thank you!

I tracked this recipe down after coming across it years ago & it was worth the effort! I made it with leftover roast chicken & it was delicious. I used very thin wheat noodles (angel hair pasta instead of rice noodles) & added them directly to the broth, cooking them first before proceeding to Step 3. Highly recommended!
I’ll make it again but add additional curry paste, garlic, ginger, shrimp and noodles, too brothy for me but of course that is a matter of taste, good flavor I just like a little more boldness.

Firstly yes it’s simple enough, but it was bland and i even added fish sauce which i think almost every Thai soup has. Secondly if i were to do it again with the red curry paste i would add at least another tsp. I do, however prefer green curry paste so i think i would do that instead. I added chicken to the soup for extra protein. I think in reality i will look for another recipe. It was good but lacking some Thai pizzazz

This was very good! It came together easily. It's all about the lemon grass which I was generous with. I was also generous with the red curry paste, using closer to a tablespoon full and I used about 1 1/2 c. mushrooms and used vegetable stock in place of chicken stock. I used shrimp, but I don't think it added much in the way of flavor; next time I will use tofu instead. I will definitely make this again. UPDATED September 2024. Still great soup. I use the Lemon grass that I get in a tube in the produce section of the grocery store; a hefty squeeze. The consistency of that is much better than when I use fresh lemon grass which is too fibrous. I also use fresh ginger, lots of it that I grated with microplane. When I’m pretty sure we will eat all of the soup in one sitting I just toss in the noodles to cook with the soup in the last five-seven mins using more veg stock in the soup base.
Such a fantastic flavor! I made w/ chicken and a mixture of different mushroooms.
Very nice.
